attempts.label: DANDI:001199
attempts.paper_title: Transcranial Focused Ultrasound Modulates Feedforward and Feedback Cortico-Thalamo-Cortical Pathways by Selectively Activating Excitatory Neurons
attempts.entry_title: Focused ultrasound and the cortico-thalamo-cortical pathway (Gao et al. 2025)
attempts.summary: No main finding of the paper could be confirmed in this data. The cell-type results for S1 and POm, including responses to repetition rate and duty cycle and the cross-area correlations, could not be tested, because the files hold spike times only, with no waveforms or cell-type labels, and only one pulse duration. The auditory cortex responses did not reproduce: 194 units against the paper's 453, with no significant dependence on repetition rate, resting on assumed voltage and trial timing for the newer sessions. The rats are fewer than the paper reports and were recorded after its preprint, so this dandiset probably holds different recordings.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Gao, Ramachandran, Yu and He (2025) on dandiset 001199, which holds sorted units (spike times only) and trial tables from 13 rats recorded in S1, POm and auditory cortex during transcranial focused ultrasound at five PRFs with 200 us pulses. It counts the rats with each pair of recorded areas, bounds the RSU and FSU counts of Fig. 4 and 5 by the untyped unit counts, and tests the auditory cortex responses across PRFs. The other RSU and FSU findings cannot be tested, as the files hold no waveforms or type labels, and the duty-cycle series is not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Gao et al. (2025) from dandiset 001199

outcomes.statement: Simultaneous S1 and POm recordings were made in 16 rats, and S1 and auditory cortex recordings in a further 12 rats.
outcomes.source: Materials and Methods, Animal surgery, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: multiunit activities were recorded from the S1 and POm (N = 16) ... To check the auditory confound, another group of rats was used (N = 12)
outcomes.notes: Simultaneous S1 and POm recordings in 6 rats (BH596, BH608, BH615, BH648, BH654, BH658), paper 16; simultaneous S1 and AC recordings in 6 rats (BH646, BH648, BH650, BH655, BH657, BH658), paper 12. Both readings of the targets (with and without the unexplained "S1-6"), and areas taken from units with more than 2,000 spikes or from every unit, give the same counts; with the 2025 cohort left out they are 2 and 0. Both counts are below the paper's, but the partial result also needs the rats to be a subset of the paper's, none extra, and the evidence goes against that. Every S1 file lists a 64-channel A1x64-Edge probe (or H9), where the paper recorded S1 with a 32-channel A1x32-Poly3. Two rats (BH648, BH658) are in both groups, where the paper's AC rats are another group. The ten rats of the two groups were recorded from August 2024 to July 2025, after the paper's preprint (June 2024), and none is among the 20 rats of dandiset 000946, the repository the paper names, whose sessions run from August 2023 to April 2024 (of the 13 rats here only BH594, which has no POm or AC recording, is there). With files of both areas in a rat, simultaneous or not, the counts are 10 and 7.
deviations: A session is a file in the 2024 cohort and a group of files sharing an identical trial table in the 2025 cohort, where each probe has its own file; the dandiset does not say this, the shared trial tables show it.
Units of BH590 and BH594 files are taken as S1, as their notes say recording at S1 and their celltype_label holds 0; BH596 and BH615 units are given the area their celltype_label holds.

outcomes.statement: High-pressure tFUS (about 170 kPa) aimed at the electrode site produces an artifact aligned with sonication that vanishes off target or at lower pressure, and extracted waveforms show tail oscillations at the 1,500 Hz PRF.
outcomes.source: Materials and Methods, Transcranial focused ultrasound stimulation, paragraph 4; Figure 2
outcomes.quote: Once the ultrasound was delivered at the desired target, high “artifact” would appear and align with the stimulation duration (Fig. 2A). To lower the pressure or move off the target could eliminate the “artifact” (Fig. 2B). The extracted spike waveform also showed oscillations at the tail due to the displacement of electrode (Fig. 2C). The frequency of the oscillations was 1,500 Hz which aligned with PRF.
outcomes.notes: The claim needs the raw voltage of the target-determination trials (about 170 kPa) and spike waveforms; the files hold sorted spike times only, and no target-determination trials. Two BH615 sessions at 10 and 15 V show a burst of detected spikes confined to 0 to 75 ms after the trial start (population rate 2.9 to 7.2 times its mean), which looks like an ultrasound-locked artefact, but neither the voltage nor the waveform tail can be examined.

outcomes.statement: In the constant-PD sessions at 3,000 Hz there were 312 RSUs and 54 FSUs in S1 and 233 RSUs and 17 FSUs in POm; at 30 Hz there were 148 RSUs and 61 FSUs in S1 and 189 RSUs and 43 FSUs in POm.
outcomes.source: Figure 4 legend
outcomes.quote: There are 312 RSUs and 54 FSUs recorded from S1, 233 RSUs and 17 FSUs recorded from POm for PRF 3,000 Hz. There are 148 RSUs and 61 FSUs recorded from S1 and189 RSUs and 43 FSUs recorded from POm for PRF 30 Hz.
outcomes.notes: RSU and FSU types come from the waveforms (IP and AHP, Methods, Neuronal type classification), which the files do not hold, and the celltype_label column holds 0 or the area in every file that has it, so the typed counts cannot be measured. A typed count is at most the untyped count of its area and condition, and the untyped counts settle the criterion. In the S1-targeted sessions at 5 V (2024) and every 2025 file (no voltage stated), there are 201 S1 and 76 POm units with more than 2,000 spikes at 3,000 Hz and 186 S1 and 53 POm at 30 Hz. The S1 and POm RSUs at 3,000 Hz need at least 280.8 and 209.7 units to be within 10%, the POm RSUs at 30 Hz 170.1, and the S1 RSUs and FSUs at 30 Hz together 188.1. So at most 4 of the 8 counts can be within 10%, where a partial result needs 6. With every voltage counted, which the claims file excludes, at most 6 could be (465 and 344 S1 units; 110 and 93 POm units, below the 209.7 and 170.1 the POm RSUs need).
deviations: The typed counts are not measured; the outcome rests on upper bounds from the untyped counts of units with more than 2,000 spikes.
The 2025 files state no voltage and are all kept, which can only raise the bounds.

outcomes.notes: The typed counts cannot be measured (see fig4-unit-counts), and the paper's control, CG1 at 3,000 Hz (claims file header and fig5b), is not in the dandiset. The untyped counts bound the sham half. Sham sessions hold 151 S1 and 37 POm units with more than 2,000 spikes; the paper's 67 POm RSUs and 67 POm FSUs each need at least 60.3, so these 2 counts cannot be within 10%. The S1 sham counts (31 and 53, needing 75.6 together) can. CG1 sessions at 300 and 4,500 Hz (11 S1 and 8 POm units) do not bound the units of control sessions at 3,000 Hz that were not deposited, so the four control counts cannot be measured, as for fig5b-cg1-control-no-response. At most 6 of the 8 counts can then be within 10%, which is what a partial result needs, so the claim cannot be decided. Had the CG1 sessions at other PRFs been counted as the control, at most 3 of 8 could be within 10%.
deviations: The typed counts are not measured; the bound on the sham half rests on the untyped counts.

outcomes.notes: 194 AC units with more than 2,000 spikes in 7 rats (paper 453; per PRF 45, 29, 42, 40 and 38 against 83, 59, 107, 104 and 100). No Kruskal-Wallis test across the five PRFs is significant at 0.01 under any reading of R (p 0.013 to 0.74); with BH654 left out the R2 tests give 0.0095 and 0.006, with every R2 mean below 100%. Against baseline only 1,500 Hz during sonication is significant, under R1 and T2 alone (mean 105.1%, uncorrected p = 6.4e-05, below 0.01 after factors 5, 10 and 15); 3,000 Hz is not (102.4%, p = 0.02 uncorrected), and no PRF is above baseline after sonication under any reading. 300 Hz has the lowest mean only under R1 during sonication with BH654 left out. Per-rat R1 means are 88 to 127%. Sham AC units give R1 means of 99.6 and 99.9% and no significant increase. Leaving out the S1-6 sessions gives the same result. Under R2 every mean is below 100%, sham included (69.8%), as R2 keeps only trials with a prestimulus spike; with BH654 left out the R2 means are 48.6 to 66.6%. The outcome rests on two assumptions about the 2025 cohort, which holds every AC file (see deviations). Trial tables and spikes span the same times (both end near 1,250 s), but the population correlogram over lags of -60 to +60 s peaks within 0 to 400 ms of the trial start in only 4 of 108 stimulated files (BH648 S1 at 4,500 Hz, z = 6.0; BH656 POm at 3,000 Hz; BH650 POm at 4,500 Hz; BH658 AC at 30 Hz), against 39 of 92 in the 2024 cohort, and no other lag fits (at most 5 files share a 0.5 s bin; the mean over 2025 files stays below z = 1). Untyped S1 units of the 2025 cohort rise under T2, the test that makes 1,500 Hz significant in AC, at 30 Hz (p = 7e-07 and 1.6e-12 in the two windows) and 1,500 Hz (2.7e-12 and 8.1e-10), means 107 to 109%, mostly in BH646 and BH648, where sham S1 units give T2 p = 0.99 and 1 and sham AC units 0.57; so the S1 spikes lock to the trial starts in at least those sessions. T1 is not significant in any 2025 S1 condition (smallest p = 0.024), so the locking is weak. At the same PRFs AC units show no increase after sonication (101.6% and 100.3%, T2 p = 0.5 and 0.34), where the paper reports one, so the failure of the pattern does not rest only on sessions whose timing is in doubt. At 300, 3,000 and 4,500 Hz the 2025 S1 units give no increase during sonication under T2 (p 0.62 to 1), and the outputs cannot tell missing responses from trial times that are not onsets.
deviations: The paper's AC group is 12 rats with S1 and AC probes; the dandiset holds AC files from 7 rats, and all 7 are used. A variant leaves out BH654, whose AC files share no session with an S1 file.
Sessions with stimulation labelled "S1-6", which nothing in the dandiset explains, are taken as S1-targeted; a variant leaves them out, with the same outcome.

Assumption. The pressure of the 2025 sessions is not stated in the files; they are taken to be at the paper's 5 V (88 kPa), as nothing in the dandiset states another voltage. The files hold no other voltage to compare, so no variant can be run.

Assumption. The trial starts of the 2025 sessions are taken as the sonication onsets. The files say nothing else, and the spikes support it in part, with locking of untyped S1 units at 30 and 1,500 Hz and correlogram peaks in 4 files (see notes). No other lag within 60 s fits, so no alternative timing can be run.
The Bonferroni factor B1 is taken as 5 (the PRFs compared with baseline in a window), with 10 (both windows) shown too; B2 is 15 (all pairs among the five PRFs and the baseline).

findings.statement: The files hold spike times only, with no spike waveforms and no RSU or FSU labels, so the paper's typing of units (IP and AHP of the waveform, k-means) cannot be repeated. Of the 20 claims on RSUs and FSUs, 18 cannot be tested and the unit counts of Fig. 4 and 5 only through upper bounds from untyped units.

The units column celltype_label is described as "label 1 = RSU, label 2 = FSU", but no file holds a 1 or a 2 (the per-file value counts give 1,272 units labelled 0, 414 POm and 773 S1). It holds 0 in the 49 files of BH590 and BH594 and the area of the unit (S1 or POm) in the 47 files of BH596 and BH615; the 133 files of the 2025 cohort have no such column.

Every stimulated file has a pulse duration of 200 us. The duty-cycle series of the paper (Fig. 7 to 9 and 10D to 10F) are not in the dandiset, nor the target-determination trials and raw voltage of Fig. 2, nor a CG1 control session at 3,000 Hz (CG1 sessions are at 300 and 4,500 Hz).

The dandiset names the paper as the description of its data, but its 13 rats were recorded from August 2024 to July 2025, after the paper's preprint of June 2024, and it holds conditions the paper does not describe (10 and 15 V, stimulation at POm, 64-channel probes with and without z-coating, 2 mm offsets). Of its rats only BH594 has a file in dandiset 000946, which the paper's Methods name as the repository of all its data and which lists 20 rats recorded from August 2023 to April 2024. Simultaneous S1 and POm recordings exist for 6 rats and S1 and AC recordings for 6, against the paper's 16 and 12.

The data_collection field gives "PRESSURE:67V" in most 2024 files whatever voltage the identifier gives (the 67 is the ultrasound duration), and the 2025 files state no pressure or voltage anywhere. The description says pressure is in the identifier, which holds for the 2024 files only.

Stimulation targets "S1-6", "NEW", "y-1" and "SEP" in the notes of 2025 files, and the identifier tags of 2024 files (coating, nocoating, NZ, C, P, 2mm, bad, break, x0y35z165), are not explained anywhere in the dandiset. Electrode locations are "unknown" in every file.

In the 2025 cohort session_start_time does not date the session. Files of two probes that share a trial table, and so are one session, have start times minutes apart, and the BH608 sham pair has start times five months apart (2025-02-06 and 2025-07-11). One file is named ses-None.
In the BH608 30 Hz session the S1 file gives stimulation at S1 and the POm file, which shares its trial table, stimulation at "SEP".
In 64 units of 16 files of the 2025 cohort the spike times are not in increasing order (one to seven places per unit). They are sorted on reading.
The files sub-BH646_ses-None and sub-BH646_ses-20250308T003900 hold the same spike trains and trial table (AC at 30 Hz); the recording is deposited twice.

The paper used two 32-channel A1x32-Poly3 probes; the S1 files here list 64-channel A1x64-Edge probes with or without z-coating, as the dandiset's description says, and four BH590 files name a device "H9". The description gives 500 trials per recording; most files hold 499 and some 113 to 480.

In the 2025 cohort, which holds every AC recording, the spikes show no more locking to the trial starts than to starts shifted by 1.25 s (true above shifted in 7 of 108 stimulated files), and the population correlogram peaks within 0 to 400 ms of the trial start in 4 of 108 stimulated files (among them BH648 S1 at 4,500 Hz), with no other lag within 60 s at which the files lock, though trial tables and spikes span the same times. In the 2024 cohort the locking is clear (0.39 against 0.13 of units modulated, 50 of 92 files; correlogram peak within 0 to 400 ms in 39 of 92). Untyped S1 units of the 2025 cohort do show a weak rise after trial starts at 30 and 1,500 Hz (means 107 to 109%), so some 2025 sessions lock. For the others, either the sessions evoked no response or their trial times are not the sonication onsets; the files cannot tell which. The data owners could state the voltage and the trial timing of the 2025 sessions.

verifications.reviewed: Round 1. The first executed notebook with the conclusion cells and the summary removed, the helper module and the claims file, with the paper. The verifier queried the archive API and tested unit_counts and normalized_rates on synthetic inputs. Its report gave its own outcome for each of the 35 claims; it disagreed with three (subjects, fig4-unit-counts, fig5-unit-counts), and gave metadata_insufficient where the record gives data_missing for 17 blocked claims.

disagreements.reason: Cell 16 finds 6 rats with simultaneous S1 and POm recordings (paper 16) and 6 with S1 and AC (paper 12). The "partially reproduced" rule needs the dataset's rats to be a subset of the paper's with none extra. The evidence goes against that: every S1 recording here uses a 64-channel A1x64-Edge probe, where the paper used two 32-channel Poly3 probes (cell 4). Two rats (BH648, BH658) sit in both groups, where the paper says "another group of rats". Only BH594, which has no POm recording, also appears in the paper's named dandiset 000946. The criterion's "none extra" condition is not checked (problem 3).

Upper bounds from cell 13 settle this without RSU/FSU types. The claims file excludes non-paper pressures, so only the 5 V files count (plus 2025 files, whose voltage is unknown). Those hold 76 POm units at 3,000 Hz (233 RSUs alone need at least 209.7), 53 POm units at 30 Hz (need at least 170.1), 201 S1 units at 3,000 Hz (need at least 280.8) and 186 S1 units at 30 Hz (RSUs plus FSUs need at least 188.1). So at least 4 of the 8 counts fail. Even counting all voltages, both POm RSU counts fail. The main count table pools the 5, 10 and 15 V sessions; the 5 V restriction appears only as a variant (problem 2).

Sham sessions hold 37 POm units in total, but 67 RSUs and 67 FSUs each need at least 60.3. CG1 sessions exist only at 300 and 4,500 Hz and hold 11 S1 and 8 POm units, below the lower bounds for control S1 FSUs (30.6), POm RSUs (49.5) and POm FSUs (37.8). So 5 or more of the 8 counts fail.

verifications.reviewed: Round 2. The full executed notebook after the round-1 revision, the helper module, the claims file and the attempt record, with the paper. The verifier agreed with 34 of the 35 outcomes and disagreed with fig5-unit-counts, which it would block as data_missing. It also listed sentences not supported by the printed outputs: the format_error finding's normalized rate of 4,224% and "one to seven places per unit" (now printed; the 4,224% is removed), the files with 400 and 149 trials (now printed), the per-rat counts at 10 and 15 V behind the BH594 sentence (now printed, and the sentence names BH594 and BH615), and those under fig11b-ac-responses.

disagreements.reason: The sham half fails only the 2 POm counts (37 units, cell 23). The other failures all come from CG1 sessions at 300 and 4,500 Hz. The paper's control, and the claims-file header, is CG1 at 3,000 Hz, and the dandiset has none. Counting other-PRF CG1 sessions does not bound units in sessions that are not deposited, so the deviation's "can only raise the bounds" does not hold. fig7-9-unit-counts and fig5b treat an absent condition as data_missing; treated the same way here, at most 2 of 8 counts are ruled out and a partial result (6 of 8) stays possible. So the outcome should be blocked (data_missing), or else carry assumed: true with the assumption stated, that the dandiset's CG1 sessions are the paper's control.

entries.name: gao-2025-001199
entries.title: Focused ultrasound and the cortico-thalamo-cortical pathway (Gao et al. 2025)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Gao, Ramachandran, Yu and He (2025) on dandiset 001199, which holds sorted units (spike times only) and trial tables from 13 rats recorded in S1, POm and auditory cortex during transcranial focused ultrasound at five PRFs with 200 us pulses. It counts the rats with each pair of recorded areas, bounds the RSU and FSU counts of Fig. 4 and 5 by the untyped unit counts, and tests the auditory cortex responses across PRFs. The other RSU and FSU findings cannot be tested, as the files hold no waveforms or type labels, and the duty-cycle series is not in the dandiset.
